answer_1.quote: We focus on the RAG evaluation on long-form answers to open-ended and non-factoid questions ... Given a question, RAG's answer, and retrieved chunks, we decompose the question into sub-questions and classify them into three types: core, background, and follow-up.
answer_1.outputs: Long-form answers to open-ended non-factoid questions

answer_2.quote: We design four metrics based on the percentage occurrence of the above scenarios: Metric #1: answer's sub-question coverage rate, ... Metric #6: longform answer's position alignment with human's writing habit.

answer_3.quote: We use the GPT-4 Judge, despite it being less effective than our proposed answer quality metrics, to compare pairs of responses ... We prompt GPT-4 with few-shot annotated examples to automatically measure the sub-question coverage.
methods: automatic sub-question coverage judgment with GPT-4

answer_4.quote: We recruit five human annotators to manually classify 200 sub-questions into three types of sub-questions, and we take the majority vote of the annotations as the ground-truth type ... Leveraging human preference data from the WebGPT Comparisons dataset, we evaluate which answer is preferred by humans.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators label sub‑question types (core, background, follow‑up) using majority vote; human preference scores are used to assess answer quality.
